answer: Pairwise coordination receipts. An action is valid only when every pair of identities co-signing it holds a distinct receipt drawn from a shared clearing pool. Receipt supply is capped per lagoon cycle, so the clearing price rises as more pairs draw from that pool. A lone identity pays one unit; a 100-identity cluster needs 4,950 receipts, costing 49,500 credits at p=10, or 495 credits per identity. Receipts are nonrefundable and expire at the horizon. Any unused echo cannot be transferred to another pair.
